title: Ember and Sigil Anew
premise: Vesper Fairweather, a mercenary bound by an old oath to a god that stopped answering, keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Ledger guild, which trades in impossible things — stolen names, bottled seasons, debts owed to the dead. When the old gods abruptly begin answering prayers again, Vesper's silent patron speaks through him, marking him as a door the divine want opened. Hunted by zealots and the guild's own creditors, he must find the Ember Gate, the last exit out of Vhalen, a country that was unmade from the maps and memories decades ago, before the long winter seals it forever. In the end, Vesper discovers he was born inside Vhalen and is himself a piece of the erased country; he chooses to burn his ledger and his god's sigil to reopen the Gate, saving others while remaining behind as the winter falls.
about_author: Casper Nystrom is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the paperwork of defunct trading companies before turning to fiction. He writes cold, ledger-precise fantasy about people who survive institutions.

chapters.title: The Silent Debtor
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the port city of Greyhollow, Vesper balances the guild's impossible accounts while quietly praying to his silent god each night, a habit he'd be mocked for. A desperate woman pays the guild in a bottled summer to ask the dead where her son went — and the dead answer for the first time in years. The emotional beat is uneasy hope curdling into dread as Vesper realizes the silence everywhere is breaking.

chapters.title: What the Gods Bought
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. His patron god finally speaks — through him, uninvited, branding a sigil on his ledger-hand and naming him 'door.' Guild mistress Ondrell sells his location to the Ashen Choir, zealots who want the door opened at any cost. Vesper flees with the woman's bottled summer as his only currency, learning from a cartographer that the way out is the Ember Gate in Vhalen, a country no one remembers. The beat is betrayal and reluctant resolve.

chapters.title: The Country That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, fractured by the god's intrusions. Crossing the wintering wastes, he reaches the borders of Vhalen and finds his own memories rearranging — a childhood village, a mother's lullaby, things that shouldn't be his. The Choir corners him at the Gate's threshold; the god demands he open himself fully. Climax: Vesper learns the truth — he was born in Vhalen, smuggled out, and is living proof the country still exists. The beat is identity shattering and reforging.

chapters.title: Ember and Sigil Anew
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, clear and his own at last. Refusing to be either god's door or the Choir's weapon, he burns the ledger — erasing every impossible debt, including his oath — and carves a new sigil of his own naming. The Gate opens for the refugees and the woman's son, but the price is Vesper's passage: a door must stay held open from one side. He remains as the long winter falls, at peace, finally belonging somewhere. The beat is sacrifice transmuted into homecoming.
